answer: For a nectar survey on a knoll and a mesa, I propose 100 tokens escrowed per voting key until 30 days after exit, plus 1 token burned daily. The ledger rejects collateral reuse and disables voting if the daily burn fails. Thus n active keys require 100n locked tokens and burn n tokens daily. Exit cannot shorten the lock, so funds cannot cycle rapidly between identities. This assumes tokens have outside value; wealthy attackers can still buy many keys. It raises Sybil costs without proving distinct humans or truthful survey data.
